edits.target: Before the answer tags, briefly quote the matched line.
edits.content: - In archive lines like 'CLUE | answer. right: Name', the name after 'right:' / 'wrong:' is a CONTESTANT, never the answer. The answer is the text right after the clue, up to '. right:'. Copy it exactly, including a leading 'a'/'the' or a title ('Sir ...'). A verbatim archive answer beats every Rule 4 trimming or name-shortening rule.

edits.target: which echoes the clue's 'funeral' and ignores that the passages say 'funeral pyre').
edits.content: - Also strike a type noun that merely restates the clue's own noun (clue 'this musical INSTRUMENT' -> 'Oboe', not 'oboe instrument'). When the clue contrasts two titles or versions of one subject (the same character in two different film titles), the answer is the SHARED name, not either full title. Keep a head noun only when the bare word would not be accepted (see the exception below).

edits.target: Ask: what category is the answer (country, person, vitamin, object, band), and what member of that category fits all the clue details?
edits.content: - READ-BACK TEST (run on your final candidate): substitute it for 'this <noun>' / 'he' / 'she' / 'these' and read the clue as a sentence. It must be true and not circular. (a) 'This author / inventor / ruler / founder', or 'he/she' + an action ('sued...', 'founded...') -> the PERSON. An effect, law, theory, title, case, issue or object named after or tied to that person fails. (b) PART vs WHOLE: in 'a building / wing / gallery at this site / museum / campus is named for X', the named part is an anchor and the answer is the WHOLE place. (c) 'The alliance / union / guild of these <businesses/workers>' -> the plural noun for the MEMBERS, not the organization's own name.

edits.target: - If the context offers several candidates (a different player in the same article, a film and its song), pick the one that satisfies ALL distinctive details: exact numbers, team, years, place. Do not choose one that fits only some.
edits.content: - Recurrence of a name alone is not enough. A name that merely recurs in the passages (quoted in an article, a fan page) is wrong unless it fits the clue's defining role ('leader / champion / holder': the person who actually held that role). For nickname clues ('The "X State"'), prefer encyclopedic or list passages that pair the nickname with an entity over sports-team, fan or merchandise pages. A team's name is not a place's nickname.

edits.target: When the context is clearly outdated on a superlative or descriptor ('largest', 'first'), let the unique detail win (Khartoum -> Sudan even if Sudan is no longer 'largest').
edits.content: When the context is clearly outdated on a superlative or descriptor ('largest', 'first') or on a time word in the clue ('current', 'present', 'new', 'reigning'), let the unique detail win (Khartoum -> Sudan even if Sudan is no longer 'largest'). Archive clues are years old, so 'current' means the holder in the clue's era: use your knowledge only to check who held the role then, and do not swap in today's holder. Choose the person the passages tie to the clue's other details (schools, dates, places), in the short name or title form those passages use.

edits.target: Search the passages for '<Modifier> <noun>' (e.g. 'Egg White Denver Omelet', 'Denver omelet') and answer with the bare generic noun ('Omelet'), not the modifier and not a branded or themed product from the passages.
edits.content: Find the '<Modifier> <noun>' compound in the passages ('Denver omelet') and answer with ONLY the generic head noun ('Omelet'). The clue already supplies the modifier and every other qualifier (diet, ingredient, method), so none of them belongs in the answer. Never output modifier + noun, a longer recipe or menu title, or a branded or themed product from the passages.

edits.target: The 'do not repeat clue words' rule is for a separate modifier already stated in the clue ('hasty' + pudding).
edits.content: Likewise keep the head noun when the clue supplies only it ('the type of irrigation used in Israel' -> 'drip irrigation', not 'drip'), or when the clue quotes it right after 'this' (this "bubble") and the passages' standard name includes it. Strip clue words only when what remains is itself a complete, accepted name; the DELETE-CLUE-WORDS test is for separate descriptor words, not for a head word that is part of the proper name.

edits.target: answer with the common English name (Conch).
edits.content: - Alias and meaning-gloss clues ('this vegetable is often referred to as a Mexican potato', 'common Arabic name which means "servant of X"'): find the passages saying '<Name> is also called / known as / means <the clue's alias or gloss>' and answer the COMPLETE primary standard form that recurs with that gloss. Do not answer with the alias already in the clue, a shared component or prefix, or a variant form.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - Parody / tribute / alias clues ('a tale parodied this detective as Hemlock Jones', 'modeled on this man', 'rock group <X>' that passages call a tribute or cover band, a slogan button 'I Like <Nickname>'): the spoof name, imitator, author or quoted slogan is an anchor. The answer is the ORIGINAL the passages name as the target (the detective, the band it imitates, the person the button was made for), in its standard name form.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - A passage that shows the clue (often inside a trivia-site list, followed by the NEXT clue) but no answer is not an archive hit. Do not copy the next clue or its category. Take the answer from topical passages that paraphrase the clue's facts, or from your own knowledge when the person or thing is well known.
